title: A sound or a video dropped on the window lands as a layer, or says why not
goal: Drag a picture onto an open document and it lands as a layer, which is the app's whole promise: everything is a layer. Drag a sound file or a video onto the same window and absolutely nothing happens. No layer, no refusal, no line under the canvas, no cursor that said no while it was in the air. Sound is a layer now and a recording is a document, so the one gesture everybody tries first should work for both, and where it genuinely cannot it has to say so out loud.
notes:
VERIFIED on 2026-09-21 by reading the drop path. Sources/Photonz/EditorState.swift:1070 addImageLayerOrOpen, which every canvas drop of a file URL goes through (EditorCanvasSurface.swift:150):

  guard let source = CGImageSourceCreateWithURL(url as CFURL, nil),
        let image = CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex(source, 0, nil) else { return }

ImageIO reads no .m4a, .mp3, .wav, .mov or .mp4, so every one of those takes the bare `return`. Not a refusal: a return. Nothing is drawn, nothing is said, nothing is logged.

That is against the rule the app already has. docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md:670 says "A refusal speaks in the same place a yes would have, and it says WHY, and it names the one thing to do", and :676 says a surface that refuses by going quiet is the thing the rule exists to stop.

From the 2026-09-21-video-audio audit rough list: "Dragging a sound file onto the window is refused: Add Sound in the Video menu is the only way in. The refusal is honest rather than silent, but it is the first thing most people will try." The audit was generous. Read at the code, it is silent.

The video half is worth doing in the same pass because it is the same line of code and a recording is a document now, so dropping an .mp4 on an open document is an obvious thing to try and does nothing.
acceptance: A sound file dropped on a document that has time lands as a sound layer at the point in time you dropped it, the same layer Add Sound would have made
A video file dropped on a document that has time lands as a clip layer
Anywhere the drop genuinely cannot be taken, it is refused in words in the place a yes would have appeared, naming what to do instead, rather than returning in silence
The drag says before you let go whether it will be taken, so nobody drops into a void
Dropping a picture keeps working exactly as it does today, including into a collage and onto a component
A walk covers dropping a sound on a document with time and a sound on one without
audit written under queue/audits/, and anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar and written into this task log if it does not

log.note: from opening-a-recording-lands-you-somewhere-you-can (2026-09-22): the recording DOOR now routes a movie asked for by Finder, the dock, a recent item or File > Open to the recording window (AppCoordinator.openFileWindow -> openRecording, flag next-opening-a-recording). Dropping one on a window was deliberately left to this task: FileDrop still refuses it. When you build this, the routing and the plain refusal wording are already there to reuse (RecordingFiles.isRecording, RecordingDoor.message).

Reproduced before building (walk /tmp/drop-media-repro-walk.json, 4 dragFile steps on the probe). CORRECTION to the task notes: the canvas is NOT silent today, it shows the no-entry pointer. All four cases log 'refused: the pointer shows the no-entry sign, no landing box, the panel says nothing' - sound over a recording, video over a recording, sound over a picture, video over a picture. So the defect is (a) two of those four should be a YES, and (b) the two that are genuinely no never say WHY. addImageLayerOrOpen's bare return is reached only from the panel/window drop paths, which refuse by type first.

left rough: a clip landing on a document the same size as the canvas is fitted to the whole canvas, so it covers the picture under it rather than arriving as a small picture-in-picture you could drag. Correct for b-roll, surprising if you wanted an overlay. Did not earn a task: nothing is broken and the right answer depends on what people actually drop.

left rough: the drop onto the window CHROME (toolbar, panel, layers list) shares the one answer with the canvas (FileDrop.carriesUsableFile -> MediaDrop.answer -> EditorState.dropMedia) but is not covered by a walk. dragFile aims at a point and every chrome point depends on the window being a particular size, so a walk over the panel would be fragile. Reasoned through and built, not walked.

left rough: a sound or a video dropped while the trim bar is up leaves the trim bar showing, still describing the clip you are no longer holding. Pre-existing: the recording window opens with the trim tool in hand (opensWithTrimInHand) and the bar does not follow the selection. Not touched by this task.

left rough: a file that is neither media nor a picture (.txt, .zip, a folder) is still refused with the no-entry pointer and no words. This pass taught only sound and video to speak. It already has the platform's own refusal sign, and there is no one move to name for a .zip, so it did not earn a task.

Adversarial review before building: the mock/task assumed a sound on ANY document should land. It cannot: addSound would give a screenshot a duration, grow a timeline and a transport under it, and turn a redlining document into a video by accident. The acceptance already scoped it ("a document that has time"), so the picture case is refused IN WORDS rather than built. The other judgment call was a video on a still picture: refusing it would have been consistent with sound, but a recording IS a document, and a .photonz let go on a canvas has always opened a window rather than landing, so it opens. That kept the shortest version: one pure answer (MediaDrop.answer), three yeses and one no, no new chrome.

A sound or a video let go on an editor window now lands or says why not, behind next-dropping-a-sound-or-a-video (on by default in Next). One pure answer in PhotonzCore/MediaDrop.swift is read by the pointer, by the sentence the canvas draws mid-drag and by what lands, so they cannot disagree: a sound on a document with time lands on the timeline at the playhead; a video lands as a clip (new PhotonzDocument.addClip, the mirror of addSound); a video on a still picture opens in its own window through the recording door; a sound on a still picture is refused with 'No timeline here for X. Open a recording first' drawn under the pointer. Verified: 16 new core tests + 6 render tests, Scripts/test.sh green, new walk drop-a-sound-or-a-video-walk green with 6 real screenshots, and the 9 other drop walks and 4 sound walks green. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-22-drop-a-sound-or-a-video.json. Commit bdce6f1f, pushed. Follow-up filed: let-go-of-a-sound-on-the-timeline-and-it-lands-a (aim the drop at a moment on the strip). Four rough items that did not clear the bar are in this log.
